chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Ash'ari, who said:

One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding the fur that is bought from the market?' He said: 'If it is guaranteed (i.e., from a slaughtered animal), there is no problem.'

key_terms.مَضْمُوناً: Guaranteed/ensured (referring to the source being halal/slaughtered)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy fur from the market if it is guaranteed to be from a slaughtered animal?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of wearing fur purchased from the market, provided it is *mazmun* (guaranteed to be from a properly slaughtered animal). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the intrinsic impurity of the hide and the requirement of proper slaughter for the meat, allowing for the use of fur in prayer when the source is verified. It reflects the practical legal reasoning applied to trade goods in early Islamic society, where market purchases often lacked explicit slaughter documentation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyra, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Al Ashary who said,

‘One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the furs, and can one buy it from the market?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was guaranteed (that it had been slaughtered), so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Ash’ariy who has said the following: “

Certain individuals of our people once wrote to abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asking, ‘What do you say about fur purchased from al-Suq (marketplace)? He (the Imam) replied, ‘If it is (lawfully) guaranteed, then it is not an offense to buy it.’”
